definitions.explanation: Describes someone who gets angry or frustrated easily and quickly.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{気|き}が{短|みじか}いので、すぐ{怒|おこ}る。
examples.english: My father is short-tempered, so he gets angry easily.

examples.japanese: {気|き}が{短|みじか}い{人|ひと}とは{仕事|しごと}がしにくい。
examples.english: It's hard to work with impatient people.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{取|と}って{気|き}が{短|みじか}くなった。
examples.english: I've become more impatient as I've gotten older.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {気|き} (temperament) + が + {短|みじか}い (short). Literally 'one's temperament is short.'

ANTONYM: {気|き}が{長|なが}い (patient, even-tempered)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- せっかち (impatient, hasty) - similar but focuses more on rushing
- {短気|たんき} (short temper) - noun form
- {短気|たんき}を{起|お}こす (to lose one's temper)

CONTRAST:
- {気|き}が{短|みじか}い: describes personality trait
- {怒|おこ}りっぽい: prone to anger (similar but more colloquial)
